# Git Basics

## Q1: How do you initialize a Git repo and make your first commit?

```bash
# Initialize a new repo
git init

# Check status
git status

# Add all files
git add .

# Commit
git commit -m "Initial commit: Android project setup"

# Add remote
git remote add origin https://github.com/user/repo.git

# Push to GitHub
git push -u origin main
```

---

## Q2: What should an Android `.gitignore` contain?

```gitignore
# Built application files
*.apk
*.aar
*.ap_
*.aab

# Files for the ART/Dalvik VM
*.dex

# Java class files
*.class

# Generated files
bin/
gen/
out/
release/

# Gradle files
.gradle/
build/

# Local configuration file (sdk path, etc)
local.properties

# Proguard folder
proguard/

# Log files
*.log

# Android Studio
.idea/
*.iml
.DS_Store
captures/
.externalNativeBuild/
.cxx/

# Keystore files (NEVER commit these!)
*.jks
*.keystore

# Google Services (e.g. APIs or Firebase)
google-services.json
```

### Key rules
| File | Why ignore? |
|------|-------------|
| `local.properties` | Contains SDK path (machine-specific) |
| `*.jks` / `*.keystore` | Signing keys — security risk |
| `google-services.json` | Contains API keys |
| `build/` | Generated by Gradle |
| `.gradle/` | Gradle cache |
| `.idea/` | IDE-specific |

## Q3: How do you clone a repo and work with remotes?

```bash
# Clone a repo
git clone https://github.com/user/android-app.git

# Clone a specific branch
git clone -b develop https://github.com/user/android-app.git

# View remotes
git remote -v

# Add a fork as a second remote
git remote add fork https://github.com/myuser/android-app.git

# Fetch from all remotes
git fetch --all

# Pull from origin
git pull origin main
```

---

## Q4: How do you view commit history?

```bash
# Simple log
git log

# One-line, compact
git log --oneline

# With graph (branch visualization)
git log --oneline --graph --all

# Last 10 commits
git log -10 --oneline

# Commits by a specific author
git log --author="Alice" --oneline

# Commits in a date range
git log --since="2024-01-01" --until="2024-06-01" --oneline

# Commits that touched a specific file
git log --oneline -- app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml

# Show what changed in a commit
git show <commit-hash>
```

---

## Q5: How do you undo changes?

```bash
# Discard changes in working directory (uncommitted)
git checkout -- app/src/main/MainActivity.kt
# OR (newer syntax)
git restore app/src/main/MainActivity.kt

# Unstage a file (keep changes)
git reset HEAD app/src/main/MainActivity.kt
# OR
git restore --staged app/src/main/MainActivity.kt

# Undo last commit (keep changes)
git reset --soft HEAD~1

# Undo last commit (discard changes)
git reset --hard HEAD~1

# Revert a commit (creates a new commit that undoes it)
git revert <commit-hash>
```

### Reset modes
| Mode | What happens |
|------|-------------|
| `--soft` | Undo commit, keep changes staged |
| `--mixed` (default) | Undo commit, keep changes unstaged |
| `--hard` | Undo commit, **discard all changes** |

---

## Q6: How do you stash changes?

```bash
# Stash current changes
git stash

# Stash with a message
git stash push -m "WIP: login screen"

# List stashes
git stash list

# Apply most recent stash (keeps it in list)
git stash apply

# Apply and drop the stash
git stash pop

# Apply a specific stash
git stash apply stash@{2}

# Drop a stash
git stash drop stash@{0}

# Stash only tracked files (not new files)
git stash --keep-index
```

### When to stash
- Need to switch branches but have uncommitted work
- Need to pull latest changes but have local edits
- Want to test something without committing

---

## Q7: How do you configure Git globally?

```bash
# Set name and email
git config --global user.name "Alice"
git config --global user.email "alice@example.com"

# Set default branch name
git config --global init.defaultBranch main

# Set default editor
git config --global core.editor "code --wait"

# Enable colored output
git config --global color.ui auto

# Set pull strategy (rebase instead of merge)
git config --global pull.rebase true

# View all settings
git config --list

# Per-repo config (overrides global)
git config user.email "work@company.com"
```
